rows.label: HIAS: total operating expenses less donated services, fiscal year to 30 September 2025

source.title: HIAS, Inc. and Related Entities, Consolidated Financial Statements for the year ended 30 September 2025 (GRF CPAs & Advisors)

rows.explainer: Total operating expenses $153,436,885 less the contributed nonfinancial assets booked as US professional fees, $18,746,450 (legal services $18,735,450 and a data security workshop $11,000, note 9) = $134,690,435. Read by all three of charityevals' HIAS models, so management and fundraising are spread over cash spending, not over law firms' billing value.

rows.label: HIAS: donated legal and professional services booked in US operations, fiscal 2025

source.title: HIAS, Inc. and Related Entities, Consolidated Financial Statements for the year ended 30 September 2025 (GRF CPAs & Advisors)

rows.explainer: Pro bono lawyers' time ($18,735,450) and a donated workshop ($11,000), recorded as contributions and as US professional fees at their fair value. Read by the US services model, which leaves it out of HIAS's cost and puts the lawyers' time in the legal branch's credit share.

rows.label: HIAS: US advocacy, community engagement and litigation cost booked in US operations, fiscal 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: The accounts report US operations as one line. The Form 990 describes the advocacy and community engagement within it (Schedule O: educating and mobilising American Jews, statewide coalitions, regional outreach in New York and Los Angeles), and the annual report HIAS's role as plaintiff in Pacito v. Trump and Global Health Council v. Trump (PDF pp. 7-8). Lobbying itself was only $12,240 (Schedule C), so the cost is mostly staff. Anchor: the Form 990's chief global policy and advocacy officer and vice-president for community engagement cost $253,493 and $235,952 with benefits (Part VII); the policy chief's role is global, so only part of that pay is US advocacy. Staff: a US team of about fifteen at roughly $120,000 each with benefits, $1.8 million; campaign, coalition and litigation support costs (Refugee Shabbat in 284 congregations, vigils in 14 states, action alerts, plaintiff work in two lawsuits) a judged $1.2 million more: about $3 million, $1.5 million (staff alone, a smaller team) to $6 million, of the line's $61.7 million in cash. Taken out of the US services model's cost and put in the advocacy model's, so each counts it once.
